candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — client rights, confidentiality, legal/ethical practice and documentation
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — HIPAA record amendment rights
candidate.educational_objective: Protect client rights by recognizing the HIPAA right to request amendment of inaccurate or incomplete health information and using the formal record-correction process.

options.A: Explain that the client has the right to request an amendment or correction through the covered entity's process and help route the request appropriately rather than independently deleting the existing record
options.B: Delete the entry immediately and remove any trace of the original documentation because HIPAA requires records to be rewritten when a client disagrees
options.C: Tell the client that HIPAA gives no right to request correction of inaccurate or incomplete health information
options.D: Advise the client to wait until a lawsuit is filed because medical-record corrections can be requested only during legal proceedings

candidate.rationale: The HIPAA Privacy Rule gives individuals the right to request amendment of protected health information in a designated record set. A covered entity must have a process to receive and act on the request; it may grant or deny the amendment under specified conditions and, if denied, the individual may submit a statement of disagreement. The bedside nurse should facilitate the formal process rather than erase or rewrite the existing record outside authorized documentation procedures.
candidate.source_claim_supported: HIPAA gives individuals a federal right to request amendment of designated-record-set PHI; amendment follows a formal covered-entity process rather than ad hoc deletion.
candidate.source_document_title: Your Medical Records; 45 CFR §164.526 Amendment of Protected Health Information
candidate.source_locator: Corrections: individuals may request a change/amendment; provider/plan must respond; 45 CFR 164.526 establishes right to request amendment and permitted denial grounds

candidate.stem: A client reviews the medical record and says, ‘This allergy entry is wrong. Please delete it from my chart right now.’ Which response by the nurse is most appropriate?
